<p>When I checked the navigation, my current location was Chungcheong Province. I needed to explain the situation to my family before I got home, but Echo’s relentless questions made it impossible to find the right moment to make the call.</p><p>Na-hyeon and Ji-hyeon wouldn’t be home on a weekday, so that was fine, but I absolutely had to tell Yu-na about what was going on.</p><p>Just then, my phone rang from an unknown number, and I realized it was a call from the Association.</p><p>“Would it be alright if I answered this call?”</p><p>“A call? You mean that vibrating device?”</p><p>“Ye—yes.”</p><p>“What is that?”</p><p>“It’s a device that allows real-time conversation even from a distance…”</p><p>“Is that so… How intriguing… Well, lesser beings have always been desperate to communicate even a little faster. Creatures without magic are…”</p><p>“Can I answer it?”</p><p>“I permit it.”</p><p>After barely cutting off Echo’s endless questions, I answered the phone.</p><p>-Hello.</p><p>-Seong-hyeon, it’s me. Han Ji-hyeok.</p><p>-Yes, Association President.</p><p>-First, I want to apologize for burdening you with such a heavy responsibility…</p><p>-…</p><p>Han Ji-hyeok’s voice sounded sincere. And only then did the reality sink in—that the fate of the Republic of Korea truly rested on my shoulders.</p><p>‘How the hell did my life end up like this?’</p><p>I was hit with belated regret—maybe I should have quit the Association the moment I picked up the Armband and gone civilian. Worry for my family’s safety gnawed at me.</p><p>-Anyway… I’ve already informed your family about the current situation.</p><p>-How much did you tell them?</p><p>-At this point, what’s there to hide? I told them everything as it is.</p><p>-Huu… Did they believe you?</p><p>-All three of them seemed surprised at first, but they accepted the situation soon after… I don’t know if this is the right thing to say, but they took it more calmly than we did…</p><p>-I see…</p><p>Sometimes I think the women in my family have more guts than I do.</p><p>‘Especially Yu-na… she’s a force to be reckoned with… in more ways than one.’</p><p>-Seong-hyeon, we’ll do our best to find a solution, so please endure a little longer…</p><p>-Yes, I understand. Then…</p><p>Echo was making a bored face in the side mirror, so I couldn’t drag out the call. I quickly ended it and continued driving.</p><p>“Human, do you love your family?”</p><p>“Yes… because they’re my family.”</p><p>“Then why don’t you enter into a formal marriage with them?”</p><p>“That… in the society of lesser beings, marriage between family members is strictly forbidden.”</p><p>“I am aware. You fear the gazes of others… How pathetic lowly creatures are….”</p><p>“…….”</p><p>I could feel my temper rising, but there was nothing I could do about it.</p><p>“Your Majesty.”</p><p>“There is no need for you to address me as Your Majesty.”</p><p>“Then what should I….”</p><p>“What do the rest of you call me?”</p><p>“‘Code Echo,’ we call you.”</p><p>Echo scratched his chin a few times, pondering, before answering with a smile.</p><p>“It is truly insolent for a lowly creature like you to decide how to address me, but I shall permit it. Revealing my true name is out of the question, so from now on, you may call me ‘Echo.’”</p><p>“I am honored…….”</p><p>Unintentionally, I had gained another privilege. If Nerus had been here, he would have been so shocked he’d fall over, staring back and forth between me and Echo.</p><p>‘I already miss that reaction.’</p><p>“Echo-nim…….”</p><p>“Speak.”</p><p>“I have a question. Why do you take interest in the human world?”</p><p>“Are you familiar with the concept of ‘gourmet’?”</p><p>“Yes, I know it refers to enjoying delicious food.”</p><p>Of course, the term “gourmet” had many meanings these days, but it seemed Echo was referring to the pure act of eating food.</p><p>‘Though I do enjoy my own kind of gourmet every day….’</p><p>“When I came here in the past, I was bound by restrictions and could not leave my castle for a very long time. Then, Nerus brought me the first lowly creature I ever met, and they gave me food. It was truly delicious. My kin have no concept of gourmet. They only swallow bland lumps of mana to replenish their power… I myself had no idea what ‘gourmet’ even was before I ate *that food*… That human brought me *that food* to my castle for ten years. After that, issues arose among my kin, and I was unable to come here for a long time—until today. I am truly pleased.”</p><p>To think the reason for his interest in humans was food… It was surprising, yet fascinating.</p><p>From Echo’s words, it seemed his species had no concept of “taste” at all.</p><p>My curiosity naturally led me to one question.</p><p>“What is *that food*?”</p><p>“Hmph.”</p><p>Echo glanced at me through the side mirror and smiled. He was already an arrogant being, but that smile seemed to carry the meaning of *‘Do you really think a lowly creature like you could understand that food?’*</p><p>Then, with that same haughty expression, he spoke solemnly.</p><p>“In your language… that food is called ‘bread.’”</p><p>“Bread…?”</p><p>Was it the same bread I knew?</p><p>“It’s not just any bread. That lowly creature offered me the ‘white bread’ that only the highest echelons were permitted to eat. In return for his efforts, I bestowed upon him countless treasures and privileges. What a nostalgic memory.”</p><p>I wasn’t sure, but even if it was a long time ago, the ‘white bread’ we commonly eat now couldn’t have been a food reserved only for the highest class.</p><p>“Pardon me, but how did that human introduce himself?”</p><p>“When we first met… he called himself a serf. His appearance was shabby, but he must have owned a vast farm and commanded slaves.”</p><p>“Ah, well…”</p><p>From my perspective, it seemed like Echo had been scammed. And by someone who, by the standards of that era, would have been treated as nothing more than a lowly ‘serf’.</p><p>It was likely that the serf had stumbled upon a Gate, entered it, met Nerus and Echo, and then, judging them to have value, offered the white bread in exchange for countless treasures.</p><p>‘To even think of scamming this monster… whoever that was, they must’ve been a real heavyweight…’</p><p>***</p><p>After that, I had many more conversations with Echo. When I asked about the language I was most curious about, Echo replied, “There is no need to learn the tongue of lowly creatures.”</p><p>Whether it was magic or something else, it seemed I would have no trouble communicating with any human I met.</p><p>As we neared my house, I pulled over to the shoulder, steeled myself with the resolve to face death, and spoke to Echo.</p><p>“There’s something I’d like to request.”</p><p>“I permit it.”</p><p>Even though I had rehearsed the words in my mind thousands of times while driving, my body trembled as I tried to speak them aloud. But I had to say it. It was something I absolutely had to do.</p><p>“My family lives in my house… It’s a weekday, so only one of them is there now, but if you stay with me, you’ll meet them all eventually… Please promise me that you will never harm my family in any way. I can’t take you home until you make that promise.”</p><p>From Echo’s perspective, this was more than just insolence—it was a statement so audacious it might warrant immediate execution. But I had to say it. If it meant I died here instead, so be it. Protecting my family was my duty as the head of the household.</p><p>Echo’s expression twisted slightly at first, but then relaxed as they answered.</p><p>“How bold… But I suppose you would be uneasy. Very well, I give you my word.”</p><p>“Thank you…”</p><p>It was just a verbal promise that could be broken at any time, but to me, even that was desperately needed.</p><p>As if sensing my lingering unease, Echo sighed deeply and said,</p><p>“Fine… I will swear it. Give me your hand.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>Echo took my outstretched right hand. Then, as they muttered words I couldn’t understand, the Armband on my wrist began to glow and vibrate, and my arm was enveloped in black smoke.</p><p>“E-Echo-nim? Your Majesty?!”</p><p>Echo ignored my words and continued muttering. When they finally finished, the black smoke vanished, and the Armband returned to normal.</p><p>“The Oath Ceremony is complete. I solemnly swear that I will bring no harm to your family, and I will consider any who turn your family into enemies as my own enemies. Does this put your mind at ease?”</p><p>“Thank you…”</p><p>I didn’t know what an ‘Oath Ceremony’ was, but it was clearly something more binding than a simple promise. It might even have actual binding power, but I couldn’t ask any more questions. I just expressed my gratitude.</p><p>I started driving again, and we finally arrived in front of my house.</p><p>This was the dream home I’d bought by pouring in every penny I had. Echo seemed surprised and intrigued by the fact that this was my house.</p><p>“Are you a noble?”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“To have a separate guest annex… It seems I’ve underestimated you.”</p><p>“It’s not a guest annex.”</p><p>“Then what is it? A villa?”</p><p>“No… It’s just my house…”</p><p>Judging by Echo’s expression, his opinion of me had dropped another notch.</p><p>After entering the password and opening the door, I heard hurried footsteps.</p><p>“Yu-na…”</p><p>Seong Yu-na was sweating nervously, but she greeted us with a smile. Then she clasped her hands together, bowed politely to Echo, and tried to kneel.</p><p>“Enough. You need not observe such formalities either.”</p><p>“Thank you…”</p><p>“So you are this man’s mother and lover. You must have suffered greatly, supporting such a pitiful husband who can’t even marry you properly for fear of public opinion.”</p><p>Yu-na couldn’t hide her shock at Echo’s explosive remarks.</p><p>Of course, the Association had never been informed of this.</p><p>‘Well… the Association doesn’t know about my incestuous relationship…’</p><p>When I silently nodded at Yu-na, she seemed to understand the situation and smiled before speaking.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291025" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Y-Your Majesty… Have you eaten? I’ve prepared a meal. Would you like some?”</p><p>Echo, who had been maintaining an indifferent demeanor, suddenly perked up with excitement.</p><p>“You know how to welcome a guest! Excellent! Bring me a feast!”</p><p>As I wondered how I’d navigate this situation going forward, I also thought that maybe, like that serf, I could tame Echo a little with food.</p><p>‘Right… Not for the nation, not for the Association… Only for my family…’</p><p>Reaffirming my sense of duty as the head of the household, I led Echo to the kitchen.</p>
